```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 88)
library(readNBS)
```

Use the bundled catalogue, manifests, and retained archives for routine
workflows. The public NBS portal supports opt-in live catalogue discovery and
Yearbook maintenance. This article covers diagnostics and deterministic parser
checks while preserving the package's fail-closed validation.

## Inspect a client before a request

Client construction is local and side-effect free; its printed summary is a
safe first diagnostic:

```{r client}
client <- nbs_client(
  timeout = 15,
  retries = 0L,
  cache_max_entries = 16L,
  cache_ttl = 300
)
print(client)
```

The defaults use HTTPS portal bases. `READNBS_BASE_URL_EN`,
`READNBS_BASE_URL_ZH`, and the comma-separated `READNBS_OBSERVATION_PATH`
environment variable can override those bindings at client construction. A
custom transport is preferable for tests because it is explicit and scoped to
one client. The cache remains per-client and in memory; clear it with
`nbs_clear_cache(client)`.

## Use installed response fixtures for deterministic discovery

`nbs_tree()` and `nbs_indicators()` are live operations by default. Installed
fixtures let their response parsers and provenance attributes be validated
locally:

```{r tree-fixture}
tree_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "tree-monthly.json", package = "readNBS"
)
tree_transport <- function(request) {
  stopifnot(identical(request$path, "new/queryIndexTreeAsync"))
  list(
    status = 200L,
    headers = list(`content-type` = "application/json"),
    body = paste(readLines(tree_file, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE),
      collapse = "\n")
  )
}
tree_client <- nbs_client(
  transport = tree_transport,
  retries = 0L,
  now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-07-29 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
tree <- nbs_tree(1, client = tree_client)
tree[c("catalog_uuid", "parent_uuid", "name", "type", "level", "is_leaf")]
```

The returned tree is a base `data.frame` with `raw_sha256`, `retrieved_at`,
and `source_url` attributes. Those attributes describe the response body and
request, while the row columns describe the catalogue node.

```{r indicators-fixture}
indicators_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "indicators-cpi-2026.json", package = "readNBS"
)
indicators_transport <- function(request) {
  stopifnot(identical(request$path, "new/queryIndicatorsByCid"))
  list(
    status = 200L,
    headers = list(`content-type` = "application/json"),
    body = paste(
      readLines(indicators_file, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE),
      collapse = "\n"
    )
  )
}
indicators_client <- nbs_client(
  transport = indicators_transport,
  retries = 0L,
  now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-07-29 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
indicators <- nbs_indicators(
  "5c7452825c7c4dcba391db5ca7f335c5",
  client = indicators_client
)
indicators[c("indicator_uuid", "catalog_uuid", "display_name", "unit")]
```

When a live response fails, distinguish transport, HTTP, JSON, API, WAF, and
schema failures in the condition class. Keep stable identities and response
validation intact while diagnosing the response.

## Diagnose invalid identities and periods

Metadata functions are the safest way to check an identity before making a
request. An unknown dataset is a typed error rather than an empty result:

```{r typed-error}
diagnostic <- tryCatch(
  nbs_dataset_valid_tuples("NBS/CN/M/NOT_A_DATASET"),
  error = function(error) {
    c(class = class(error)[[1L]], message = conditionMessage(error))
  }
)
diagnostic
```

For a real request, check that the stable ID comes from
`nbs_catalogue()`/`nbs_dataset_catalogue()`, use
`nbs_dataset_valid_tuples()` for filters, and request a bounded period. Common
typed conditions include `nbs_unknown_series_error`,
`nbs_unknown_dataset_error`, `nbs_dataset_filter_error`, `nbs_period_error`,
`nbs_range_error`, `nbs_manifest_gap_error`, and
`nbs_dataset_cardinality_error`. A changed portal response can additionally
produce transport, HTTP, JSON, API, or schema conditions.

## Parse a retained Yearbook route offline

Normal Yearbook parsing works on already acquired local HTML. The contents
fixture below exercises discovery and target matching:

```{r yearbook-routes}
index_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "yearbook-2011-left.html", package = "readNBS"
)
index_html <- paste(
  readLines(index_file, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE),
  collapse = "\n"
)
routes <- nbs_yearbook_routes(
  index_html,
  yearbook = 2011,
  index_url = "https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/ndsj/2011/left.htm"
)
routes[c("source_yearbook", "family", "source_table", "source_url", "schema_era")]
```

The merged-header table fixture focuses on rowspan/colspan geometry while
leaving the complete official table outside its scope. The example uses the
discovered route and overrides only the geometry contract for the fixture:

```{r yearbook-parser}
table_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "yearbook-table-merged.html", package = "readNBS"
)
table_html <- paste(
  readLines(table_file, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE),
  collapse = "\n"
)
fixture_route <- routes[routes$source_table == "3-1", , drop = FALSE]
fixture_route$expected_columns <- 3L
fixture_route$expected_min_rows <- 4L
fixture_route$header_rows <- 3L
parsed <- nbs_yearbook_parse_table(
  table_html,
  fixture_route,
  retrieved_at = as.POSIXct("2026-08-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
parsed[c(
  "source_yearbook", "source_table", "reference_year", "measure",
  "value", "raw_value", "source_url", "raw_sha256"
)]
```

Maintainers should compare the real table geometry with the frozen target
manifest before updating an archive. A live contents-page request is reserved
for that maintenance workflow:

```{r live-maintenance, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive()) {
  discovered <- nbs_yearbook_discover_live(
    2011,
    client = nbs_client(timeout = 15, retries = 2L)
  )
  head(discovered)
}
```

Live discovery returns data for maintainer review. Acquisition and
normalisation scripts in a source checkout then freeze the document, verify
its hash, validate the table shape, and review the resulting diff before a
manifest or archive is changed.

## What to include in a bug report

Email chartwellmacro@gmail.com with:

* package version and R version;
* stable series or dataset ID, language, date range, and exact filters;
* the condition class and message;
* `route`, `source_vintage`, `manifest_version`, and source URL when a result
  was returned; and
* a minimal reproducible example using an installed fixture or an injected
  transport where possible.

Never include passwords, tokens, private URLs, or credentials. See the
[contributing guide](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readNBS/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
and [security guidance](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readNBS/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
for repository support and responsible disclosure.
